episodes.201559: Daytime heating combined with higher moisture east of a dryline and upper level northwest flow across the northern and central Rockies and Great Plains resulted in the development of severe storms with large hail across Colfax, Union and far northeast Harding Counties during the late afternoon and evening hours before exiting into West Texas after midnight. A more potent shortwave at the base of an upper low over the central U.S. and Canadian border moved across the central and southern Great Plains on June 8th resulting in the development of strong to severe storms across northeast and east central NM during the mid afternoon and evening hours until exiting into Texas at around sunset. Finally, a 61 mph wind gust was observed at Raton Crews Airport during the evening hours of June 11th due to a nearby thunderstorm.||These storms pushed a backdoor front and higher moisture south and west across eastern and central NM resulting in the development of another round of strong to severe storms across these parts of the state during the afternoon hours of June 9th. Storms organized into a convective line across eastern New Mexico during the evening hours producing damaging wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph across parts of the east central plains. This complex of storms exited into Texas just before midnight. Daytime heating combined with an upper level disturbance moving into southern New Mexico resulted in the development of some strong thunderstorms across the higher terrain. Thunderstorms across the Sacramento Mountains dropped heavy rainfall in a short period of time on the South Fork and Salt burn scars around Ruidoso resulting in some flash flooding and debris flows in the Upper Canyon area just west of downtown Ruidoso. These storms combined into a larger complex of storms over Chaves County before exiting into West Texas during the early evening hours.||Key Impacts: Hail, Severe Thunderstorm Wind Gust, Flash Flooding, Debris Flow.
episodes.201599: An upper disturbance brought mainly sub-severe storms except for at Wilmington International Airport.
episodes.201609: A shortwave trough swung through Eastern NC during the afternoon hours. A batch of showers and thunderstorms moved quickly northeastward, with one particular storm becoming severe and producing wind damage along the coast.
episodes.201624: A triple point between an occluded, cold and warm fronts extending south from a surface low across James Bay Canada moved across northern NY during the afternoon hours of June 10th. The airmass was marginally unstable with a few showers and an isolated thunderstorm or two. One thunderstorm briefly intensified and may have interacted with a sea-breeze front off of Lake Champlain that produced a very brief EF0 tornado in Beekmantown with several trees downed, some yard objects lifted and moved and a partial unstable roof torn off a house.
episodes.201628: A line of thunderstorms produced localized wind damage over a small portion of eastern West Virginia.
episodes.201631: A low pressure system stationed along the Hudson Bay allowed for central Pennsylvania to experience a brief period in the warm sector during the afternoon hours of June 9, 2025 ahead of a mid-level trough. This trough aided in large-scale ascent ahead of a surface cold front that aided in supercell development across western and central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening with the trailing cold front, allowing for a second round of thunderstorms containing locally heavy rainfall and some severe thunderstorms that produced wind damage. Locally heavy rainfall in Altoona led to multiple roadways in and around the city becoming impassable with States Road quickly being washed out by the rainfall. Later in the evening, two supercells formed across the central mountains of Pennsylvania, with the southernmost one producing large hail in Mifflin County and producing widespread tree damage in northern Huntingdon County. The northernmost supercell produced multiple trees and wires down in Milesburg. An isolated severe thunderstorm also knocked down two trees into a residence in northern Perry County, with no injuries reported. Heavy rainfall also caused isolated instances of flash flooding in central Bedford County and northern Huntingdon County, with flooding reported in Perry County during the early morning hours of June 10th.
episodes.201748: A frontal boundary stalled across the Piedmont of North Carolina. Along and out ahead of this stalled boundary a mesoscale convective complex developed during the early morning hours of the 10th and raced east impacted the coastal waters along the Crystal Coast. A few of these storms became strong to severe in nature bringing strong and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.201750: A frontal boundary stalled across the Piedmont of North Carolina. Along and out ahead of this stalled boundary a mesoscale convective complex developed during the morning  hours of the 10th in South Carolina and raced east-northeastward impacted the coastal waters along the Crystal Coast. A few of these storms became strong to severe in nature bringing strong and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.201763: Thunderstorms developed along the higher terrain before slowly drifting across portions of the eastern panhandle of West Virginia. Thunderstorms produced localized rainfall amounts of two to five inches which resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.201912: The same slow moving long wave trough caused severe weather on preceding days helped trigger and organize another broken line of severe convection in the Midlands of SC on June 9th. Sufficient low level shear and strong instability helped produce two tornadoes along with a swath of scattered damaging winds into the central Midlands.
episodes.202291: A squall line become dominated by outflow and only produced on report of a severe wind gust at an ASOS but no damage followed by a few gusts over the marine environment.
episodes.202652: Thunderstorms that originated in the high terrain of New Mexico congealed into a line of thunderstorms as they tracked east and impacted the southwestern Texas Panhandle. The main impact was from wind gusts up to 60mph.
episodes.203190: A slow-moving cold front arrived during the evening hours, moving into a very moist environment with strong wind shear. With some sunshine around during the afternoon ahead of the front, there was some modest instability. A few storms became strong to severe with locally damaging winds and heavy rain. One man was injured after getting struck by lightning while closing windows on his enclosed porch.
episodes.203196: An upper level low and remnant MCVs produced several rounds of heavy rain and training storms that produced flash flooding for a few day across the region, mainly across Central Texas.
episodes.203272: Marine thunderstorms produced strong winds near Galveston Bay.
episodes.203273: A funnel cloud developed near Liverpool and drew media attention.
episodes.203276: A cold front/outflow boundary, coupled with vorticity maxima in the northwesterly flow aloft, resulted in the development of severe thunderstorms in the Permian Basin of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico during the evening and overnight hours on June 9th. Supercells formed initially, but storms eventually grew upscale later that night. These storms produced multiple instances of severe winds (especially the MCS) and large hail. A landspout was also reported in Martin County.
episodes.203278: A cold front/outflow boundary, coupled with vorticity maxima in the northwesterly flow aloft, resulted in the development of severe thunderstorms in the Permian Basin of West Texas and Southeast New Mexico during the evening and overnight hours on June 9th. Supercells formed initially, but storms eventually grew upscale later that night. These storms produced multiple instances of severe winds (especially the MCS) and large hail. A landspout was also reported in Martin County.
episodes.203302: A weak disturbance out of South Carolina brought a batch of showers and storms into the Sandhills and Coastal Plain of central North Carolina during the afternoon. This led to a few storms producing wind damage in Cumberland county. Additionally, a stalled front over the Piedmont produced isolated storms in the late evening hours, which produced some large hail and wind damage in Stanly County.
episodes.203446: A stationary boundary (and associated surface convergence), coupled with upslope flow, led to the development of severe thunderstorms during the afternoon of June 10th as a shortwave approached Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. Initial isolated to scattered storms tended to produce large hail and damaging winds. Upscale growth occurred during the evening/overnight hours, and the primary threat shifted to damaging winds (similar to what happened during the evening of June 9th).
episodes.203447: A stationary boundary (and associated surface convergence), coupled with upslope flow, led to the development of severe thunderstorms during the afternoon of June 10th as a shortwave approached Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. Initial isolated to scattered storms tended to produce large hail and damaging winds. Upscale growth occurred during the evening/overnight hours, and the primary threat shifted to damaging winds (similar to what happened during the evening of June 9th).
episodes.203577: A front was stalled across south GA with SW steering flow over the local area. Southwest steering flow, diurnal instability and high moisture fueled scattered afternoon thunderstorms, some of which became severe in the afternoon and early evening near the east coast where boundaries collided as a short-wave trough passed overhead.
episodes.203578: A front was stalled across south GA with SW steering flow over the local area. Southwest steering flow, diurnal instability and high moisture fueled scattered strong to severe storms with the passage of short-wave trough energy aloft.
episodes.203651: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Tulsa County during the late afternoon of the 10th, resulting in wind damage and hail up to penny size.
episodes.203866: A surface low formed along a stationary front across central Virginia during the evening of June 8. This low moved east overnight into the early morning hours of June 9. Scattered storms formed in response to the surface low and moved across portions of the lower Chesapeake Bay and James River in the early morning hours of June 9, producing gusty winds. Another isolated storm moved across the lower Chesapeake Bay during the afternoon of June 9, producing gusty winds.
episodes.204008: Scattered afternoon summertime thunderstorms developed in portions of central and north Georgia. Isolated damaging wind reports were found.
episodes.204034: A mid-level shortwave trough generated thunderstorms over the Big Bend region, and these storms moved into South-Central Texas. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.204084: A cold front moved through the area on the ninth which brought easterly upslope flow well into eastern New Mexico. Thunderstorms initially developed off of the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico and propagated southeastward into West Texas. Sufficient atmospheric instability was present to allow these storms to grow upscale into a mesoscale convective system as it crossed into West Texas. A couple of severe thunderstorm reports were observed as this complex moved across the South Plains.
episodes.204104: Severe thunderstorms affected parts of the Concho Valley and Northern Edwards Plateau. There were a few reports of very large hail.
episodes.204190: A westward push of the dryline toward the Rio Grande Valley combined with a weak upper trough moving along the International Border brought scattered showers and thunderstorms to parts of Hudspeth county with a wind gust to 66 mph reported.
episodes.204343: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed along a cold front and within the warm sector of an approaching system. Favorable shear, along with forcing from the cold front helped to develop severe storms that also resulted in a confirmed tornado in the western Southern Tier. Additionally, a very moist atmosphere was present within the systems warm sector, helping to contribute to heavy rainfall with showers and thunderstorms. Some of the heavy rain that developed across the western Southern Tier, combined with antecedent conditions caused flash flooding in Allegany County.
episodes.204370: A summertime pattern continued over the area with scattered thunderstorms.  A few storms were severe with impacts to trees and power lines.

episodes.204504: A slow-moving cold front interacted with a very unstable airmass, resulting in scattered thunderstorms across north Mississippi during the evening of June 9, 2025.  One storm became severe in Pontotoc County with large hail.
episodes.204531: A mid-upper level disturbance traversing the Southeast in advance of a longwave trough encountered a moderately unstable environment, leading to severe thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts across Southeast Georgia.

episodes.204860: Northwest flow aloft regime continued to be in place on June 9th with an upper level ridge center west of the local forecast area. This pattern carried developing storms from NW to SE across the area late in the afternoon. Sufficient instability aided in thunderstorm enhancement which resulted in severe wind gusts in a few coastal areas.
episodes.204868: A north/south oriented trough axis extended from the Great Lakes to the Florida Panhandle and a ridge was centered over the Desert Southwest encompasses the rest of the country. That put the CWA right between both features. The frontal boundary associated with the trough stalled along the northern Gulf Coast. That front was the initial focal point for convection to begin developing early in the afternoon. That activity was been able to capitalize on very high instability. Quite robust thunderstorms produced multiple severe wind gusts.
